F1-npe-catch-exception.reason: The fork's caught NullPointerException omits the JDK's helpful detail message ("Cannot invoke \"String.length()\" because \"<local1>\" is null"). Left out on purpose (D11): the helpful message names the JDK's own internal variable slots, and no course page shows it. Apart from the differences listed here, the runtime errors this suite checks carry the JDK's text: array and String indexes, number parsing and casts since patch teavm-0009; division by zero since teavm-javac-0102 (StrictArithmetic); ArrayList and StringBuilder indexes and negative array sizes since teavm-0012.

F1-unused-throwing-read.reason: TeaVM's optimizer deletes the array read a[3] because its result is never used, so the exception it would have thrown never happens; known limitation of the fork's current optimizer settings, no fix planned. An unused cast is dropped the same way (F1-unused-cast).

F1-unused-cast.reason: TeaVM's optimizer drops the cast (String) o because its result is never used, so the ClassCastException the JDK throws never happens; a cast whose result is used throws with the JDK's text (G7-cast-temp). Known limitation of the fork's current optimizer settings, no fix planned.

F3-two-scanners.reason: With piped stdin the JDK's first Scanner reads ahead, past the line it returns, so the second Scanner finds nothing left; the fork's Scanner reads only as far as the line it needs (teavm-0005 reads input lazily, one line at a time), so the second one still sees "two". Known limitation; the course reads stdin through one reader per program.

F3-readln-then-scanner.reason: Same cause as F3-two-scanners: with piped stdin the JDK's IO.readln reads ahead, past the line it returns, so the Scanner opened after it finds nothing and the program prints -1; the fork's IO.readln reads only its own line, so the Scanner still sees 7. Known limitation; the course reads stdin through one reader per program.

F4-format-grouped-float.reason: The fork's Formatter does not implement the %e conversion, throwing UnknownFormatConversionException where the JDK prints scientific notation; known limitation, the course's formatting material never uses %e.

G7-array-store.reason: The fork does not check stores into an array: storing an Integer into a String[] held as Object[] throws no ArrayStoreException, so the catch never runs and nothing is printed where the JDK prints "caught". The store only looks harmless because this case never reads the element back; reading it back traps, and no catch can handle a trap (G7-array-store-read-back). Listed on purpose (Task 7); the course never stores into a covariant array.

G7-array-store-read-back.reason: The same unchecked store as G7-array-store, with the element read back: the store goes through ("stored") where the JDK throws ArrayStoreException, and reading the element back through the String[] traps inside a catch (RuntimeException) that cannot handle it, so the run ends in a trap with nothing after "stored". Listed on purpose (Task 7); the course never stores into a covariant array.

R11-math-log.reason: The x86-64 JDK only (D112). The fork's Math.log is fdlibm's, as StrictMath.log is on every platform (D33), and so is the pinned JDK's on arm64 (the Mac), where Math.log equals StrictMath.log on all 20,000 of this case's values. The same pinned JDK on x86-64 Linux computes Math.log another way, as Math's Javadoc allows (within 1 ulp of the exact result): 458 of the 20,000 differ from StrictMath.log by exactly 1 ulp (the first is Math.log(0.0822), -2.4985999769200027 where StrictMath.log gives -2.498599976920003), so the hash differs while Math.log(10) and Math.log(0.5) agree. Measured on the first public CI run (ubuntu, x86-64) and with the pinned Linux JDK under x86-64 emulation on the Mac, where -Xint gives the same.

R11-hex-float-literal.reason: The fork's javac compiles every hexadecimal floating-point literal (0x1p0, 0x1.8p1, 0x1p-52) to NaN instead of the value the JDK's javac gives, and its Double.parseDouble/Double.valueOf reject a hex string with NumberFormatException where the JDK parses it; known limitation, to be fixed only when a course example needs hex float literals (D34).

R11-math-ulp.reason: TeaVM's own TMath.ulp(double) masks the exponent bits with 0xEFF0000000000000L instead of 0x7FF0000000000000L, so ulp(1.0) comes out many orders of magnitude too large; ulp(1e10), ulp(1.0f) and ulp(0.0) already agree with the JDK by coincidence of that same mask. Upstream TeaVM bug, unrelated to any patch in this series; known limitation, to be fixed only when a course example needs it (D34).
